Agent Studio Essentials›Build Your First Genie

Build your first Genie in Agent Studio

Foundational 120 minutes Lab 1 of 1
Introduction

In this lab, you'll act as automation engineer for Anitech who sets up an IT-support Genie (AI Agent), provides it with company knowledge, and gives it the skills to create and read Kanban support tickets.

Ae
Automation engineer
Workato builder · Anitech

Anitech's IT team is drowning in routine tickets; you're building the Genie that will triage them.

The question

Can a Genie handle a real IT support conversation end-to-end by answering questions, escalating when needed, and taking action?

You'll learn how to

  • Sign in to a Workato workspace via Okta and review provisioned project resources
  • Configure a Genie's chat interface, name, and job description in Agent Studio
  • Grant an end-user group access to a Genie and interact with it via Workato Go
  • Test a Genie in test mode and read its decision trace
  • Add a knowledge base sourced from a connected data source
  • Explore a ticket-tracker app's statuses, priorities, and access model
  • Create a connection and build skills that create, retrieve, and list tickets
  • Use AIRO to update a skill's description

What you'll need

  • A Workato workspace with access to Agent Studio and AIRO
  • A Workato project where you will build your Genie
  • A Workato Go instance for interacting with your Genie
  • Okta as an identity provider for managing access to Workato, Genies, and Workato Go
  • Kanban as a ticket-tracking application
  • The credentials email titled "World of Workato 2026 - Your Training Login Credentials" from mailer@workato.com
Phase 1

Agent Studio

1.1

Sign in and review your workspace

Anitech's help desk queue sits ten tickets deep, and every one of them waited on a human first. Before you touch Agent Studio, you need to log into the workspace where the Genie that changes that will actually live.

Overview

Signing in through Okta lands you in the AI Hub, where Agent Studio and your assigned project already exist. The project's FileStorage folder holds prompt.md — the job description you paste into the Genie in Task 2.1, not something you draft from scratch.

Key insight

Why the job description ships pre-written — Agent Studio's own generated description is a reasonable start, but `prompt.md` reflects a description already reviewed for Anitech's tone and boundaries. Task 6.1 is where AIRO helps you keep later descriptions equally deliberate.

Detailed steps 8 steps

There's no earlier build to connect to — this is where the lab starts. Task 1.2 sets up the folders that keep everything you create from here on organized, and Task 2.1 is where the job description you download here actually gets used.

  • Open the credentials email from mailer@workato.com, subject "World of Workato 2026 - Your Training Login Credentials," and note your assigned username and password.
  • Sign in to Okta at https://training-workatolabs.okta.com with those credentials.
  • Launch the Workato workspace provisioned for you.
  • In the left navigation, under AI Hub, choose Agent studio.
  • Choose Projects in the left navigation, then open your assigned project.
  • Navigate to Tools → FileStorage → prompts.
  • Choose prompt.md, then choose Download.
  • Open the downloaded file and review the job description you'll use in Task 2.1.
Verify prompt.md downloads successfully and you can open its contents.
1.2

Create folders

Three folders are about to hold every connection, knowledge base, and skill you build today — get the naming right now and Phase 5 skips a detour.

Overview

You create three top-level folders in your project — Connections, Knowledge, and Skills — each scoped to hold one category of asset your Genie uses later. Nothing beyond folder creation happens in this task.

Detailed steps 5 steps

The Genie you build in Task 2.1 needs somewhere to put its connection, knowledge base, and skills — these three folders are that home, created before any of those assets exist. Nothing here is Genie-specific yet; it's the same folder discipline any Workato project uses.

  • Navigate to your project in the Workato workspace.
  • At the top right, choose Create → Folder.
  • Name the folder Connections.
  • Repeat to create a folder named Knowledge.
  • Repeat to create a folder named Skills.
Verify your project's asset list shows three folders: Connections, Knowledge, and Skills.
Phase 2

Build Your First Genie

2.1

Set the genie configuration

Anitech doesn't have an IT Genie yet — it has ten open tickets and a job description sitting in your downloads folder. Time to give the description somewhere to live.

Overview

Creating a Genie through Create → Genie starts a build flow: name it, pick Workato Go as its chat interface, then replace the generated job description with the reviewed one from prompt.md. Renaming with your project number and initials keeps Genies distinguishable once several trainees build in the same workspace.

Heads up

Shared workspace, shared names — every trainee builds in the same workspace today. Skipping the `XXXYY` prefix means your Genie is indistinguishable from twenty other "IT Support genie" entries.

Genie naming convention
FieldValue
Rename toXXXYY Casey
XXXyour assigned project number
YYyour initials
Detailed steps 8 steps

This is the task where Casey stops being folders and starts being a Genie — a name, a chat interface, and the job description from Task 1.1 all land here. Task 2.2 is what makes this Genie reachable by an actual end user; without it, everything built here stays invisible outside Agent Studio.

  • In your project, choose Create → Genie.
  • For "What would you like your genie to help with?" enter: I want to create an IT Genie that can handle IT requests for my company.
  • Choose Start building.
  • Rename the generated Genie following the naming convention above.
  • In the Triggers section, choose Add, then select Workato Go as the chat interface.
  • Review the generated Job Description.
  • Replace the generated text with the contents of prompt.md that you downloaded in Task 1.1.
  • Choose Save, then choose Exit to return to the Genie overview.
Verify your Genie appears with the XXXYY Casey name, Workato Go as its chat interface, and the pasted job description saved.
2.2

Configure user access

Casey exists, but nobody outside Agent Studio can reach it yet — the access list is still empty.

Overview

End-user access to a Genie is opt-in by group, not by individual — you add the group that maps to your assigned Okta persona, then start the Genie so Workato Go can serve it. Anyone outside that group won't see the Genie at all.

Heads up

Access is opt-in by group — your end user only sees Genies made available to the group assigned in Okta. If Casey doesn't appear in Workato Go later, this is the first place to check.

Detailed steps 5 steps

Casey exists after Task 2.1, but nobody outside Agent Studio can reach it yet — this task is what changes that. Task 2.3 is the first real test of the access granted here: get the end-user group wrong, and Casey won't appear in Workato Go at all.

  • Scroll up and choose End user settings, then confirm End user access is selected.
  • Choose Add end-user groups.
  • Select the end-user group that corresponds to your assigned Genie Access Group (named in your credentials email), then choose OK.
  • Choose Add.
  • Choose Start Genie in the upper right corner.
Verify Start Genie is active and your assigned end-user group appears under End user access.
2.3

Interact with the Genie

Casey is live. The real test isn't the build screen — it's whether an actual end user can start a conversation.

Overview

Workato Go is the chat surface end users reach Casey through. Starting a new conversation and asking Casey a question before it has a knowledge base — like asking how to use the Anitech office kitchen coffee machine — shows you what a Genie sounds like before it has real company knowledge behind it.

Note

Why the answer sounds so generic — Casey hasn't been provided with Anitech's own content yet. Expect a generic answer, or an honest "I don't have that information" — both are correct behavior for this task, not a bug.

Detailed steps 4 steps

This is the first time Casey talks to an actual end user instead of you in the build screen — and deliberately over a question with no real answer yet. Task 2.4 goes behind that same kind of exchange to show you why the answer came out the way it did.

  • Navigate to Workato Go using the link in your credentials email, then authenticate.
  • Choose Genies in the left navigation.
  • Find your Genie on the page and choose Chat with <genie name>.
  • Ask Casey how to use the coffee machine in the Anitech kitchen.
Verify Casey responds to a message sent from Workato Go.
2.4

Test the Genie

Anitech's IT team needs to see Casey think, not only answer — decision traces are how you'd debug a bad response later.

Overview

Test mode surfaces the Genie's reasoning behind each reply — which tools it called and why — without touching the live Workato Go conversation. Returning to test mode later starts a clean trace with New test.

Detailed steps 5 steps

The ungrounded answers from Task 2.3 are exactly what Phase 3 exists to fix — but before changing anything, this task shows you how to see a Genie's reasoning at all. Every knowledge base and skill added from here forward can be checked the same way: through test mode's decision trace.

  • Return to the Genie overview in Workato.
  • Choose Edit, then choose Test.
  • Choose Start Testing.
  • Type a message such as "What is the Anitech policy for a work from home monitor?" and send it.
  • Choose the message from your chat interaction to view the Genie's decision trace for that reply.
Verify the test mode chat shows a decision trace for at least one message.
Phase 3

Knowledge Bases

3.1

Add a knowledge base to your Genie

Casey still can't answer a single Anitech-specific question — the fix isn't a better prompt, it's a knowledge base.

Overview

Creating a knowledge base backed by the pre-connected IT Onboarding Wiki data source gives Casey Anitech-specific content to search, instead of relying on what the underlying model already knows. The knowledge base's name and description both matter — they're what tell the Genie when to use it.

Key insight

Name and description are instructions, not labels — the Genie decides whether to search a knowledge base based on what its name and description say it contains. A vague description means Casey guesses wrong about when to use it.

Knowledge base
FieldValue
NameOnboarding Wiki
LocationKnowledge folder
DescriptionContains articles that describe how employees can start using IT services and technologies.
How you will add dataChoose from connected data sources
Data sourcesIT Onboarding Wiki
Detailed steps 5 steps

Casey answered your coffee-machine question in Task 2.3 from general training data alone — technically working, but useless for anything Anitech-specific. This task is where that changes: a knowledge base gives Casey something real to search instead of guessing. Once this is implemented, Phase 4 shifts focus entirely to the Kanban side of the build, so this is the last knowledge-base task before skills take over.

  • Return to your Genie's Build mode.
  • In the Knowledge bases section, choose Add, then choose Create knowledge base.
  • Enter the name, location, description, and data source from the Config above.
  • Choose Create knowledge base.
  • Switch back to Workato Go, start a new thread with your Genie, and ask an onboarding question such as "How do I set up my new laptop?"
Verify Casey answers an Anitech-specific onboarding question using content from the Onboarding Wiki knowledge base.
Phase 4

Explore the Kanban Ticket Tracker

4.1

Get to know the Kanban ticket tracker

Before Casey can create or read a single ticket, you need to understand the board it's about to touch.

Overview

Signing in to the Playground environment and switching to Kanban through the app picker menu lets you explore the same ticket-tracker app your skills call in Phase 5. The IT Support board's statuses, priorities, and per-employee access model become hard constraints the moment you wire a connection to it.

Questions to answer
FieldValue
Question 1In the IT Support Kanban board, what are the three possible statuses of a ticket?
Question 2What are the five possible priorities of tickets?
Question 3What are the names of the IT Support employees you see in the Quickchange Persona dropdown menu?
Question 4Can all IT Support employees see all IT tickets?
Question 5What is the difference between a Reporter and an Assignee?
Question 6Can the same IT Support employee be both the Reporter and the Assignee?
Question 7If an end user creates a ticket through a Genie instead of an IT Support employee, what shows in the ticket's Reporter field?
Question 8Of the three roles — Guest, Watcher, and Writer — which one can change a ticket's status?
Question 9The most common Issue Type is "Task." True or false?
Question 10A ticket's Labels field can hold more than one key/value pair. True or false?
Detailed steps 3 steps

Casey can answer questions now, but Phase 5 is about to give it the ability to act on Kanban tickets — and none of those skills will make sense without seeing the board first. This task has no build step at all; what you confirm here is what every skill starting with Task 5.1 has to respect.

  • Sign in to the Playground environment using your assigned credentials.
  • Use the App picker menu at the top left of the screen to confirm you're in Kanban.
  • Answer the questions above by exploring the Kanban ticket tracker app directly.
Verify you have an answer for all 10 questions, drawn only from what you observed directly in the Kanban board, the Quickchange Persona menu, and a ticket's own fields. Check your answers against the Appendix at the end of this lab once you've tried them yourself.
Phase 5

Skills

5.1

Create a connection

Every skill Casey gets from here forward calls Kanban through the exact same door — build that door once.

Overview

One Kanban connection, authenticated with your Playground credentials under Credentials (preconnect-friendly), is reused by every skill you create in this phase. The naming convention — project number, CON, RW, app name — is what makes a connection identifiable once a workspace has dozens of them.

Heads up

This connection authenticates as the IT Service Account persona in Kanban, not as you — every ticket your skills create or retrieve happens under that identity, which is exactly what Task 4.1's Reporter-field question was pointing at.

Connection naming convention
FieldValue
NameWOW-XXX | [AGENT-STUDIO] : CON : RW : Kanban
XXXyour assigned project number
AuthenticationCredentials (preconnect-friendly)
Detailed steps 8 steps

Every skill in the rest of Phase 5 needs to talk to Kanban, and this connection is the one door all three of them use. Task 5.2 is the first skill built on top of it — get the authentication persona wrong here, and every ticket those skills touch will be wrong too.

  • Navigate to the Connections folder in your project.
  • Choose Create → Connection.
  • Search for and select Kanban.
  • Name the connection following the convention above.
  • Confirm Location is set to the Connections folder of your project.
  • Set Authentication to Credentials (preconnect-friendly).
  • Enter your unique Playground Pseudonym, Session Code, and Password.
  • Choose Connect.
Verify the Kanban connection shows a successful, active connection status.
5.2

Create a skill to create a Kanban ticket

Casey can talk about a problem all day — creating the actual ticket is the one action that gets an Anitech end user unstuck.

Overview

A skill named for the project's SKILL : 001 convention wraps the Kanban Create Kanban ticket action behind trigger questions and an input schema Casey fills from the conversation. The Response step's Result field, switched to Formula mode, is what lets the skill hand a structured value back to the Genie instead of raw text.

Heads up

Confirmation is the safety valve — setting "Require user confirmation" to Yes here means Casey always checks with the end user before filing a ticket on their behalf; Tasks 4.3 and 4.4 turn this off because reading data carries no side effect.

Skill naming and trigger questions
FieldValue
NameWOW-XXX | [AGENT-STUDIO] : SKILL : 001 : Create Kanban Ticket
LocationSkills folder
Require user confirmation before executing this skill?Yes
When should this skill run?Create new Kanban ticket to track helpdesk requests that could not be solved in chat. When to use: the user says they want to create a ticket; the user says they want to escalate; you have tried a few troubleshooting steps and can't solve the user's problem. Examples: "hey i'd like to submit a ticket for this problem" · "can we escalate my request"
Input fields (What input does this skill need to run?)
FieldValue
ProjectKeyString, required — use "IT" for all IT-related entries
SummaryString, required — maximum 40 characters
DescriptionString, required
PriorityString, required — "Lowest", "Low", "Medium", "High", or "Highest"
Issue_TypeString, required — default "Task"
StatusString, required — initial status is "To do"
Due_DateDate, required — maximum one week from today
LabelsList of Key/Value string pairs, optional
Output field (What information does this skill send back?)
FieldValue
resultString, optional
Recipe data → action field mapping
FieldValue
Project keyStep 1 output → Parameters → Project key
SummaryStep 1 output → Parameters → Summary
DescriptionStep 1 output → Parameters → Description, appended with Step 1 output → Context → User name / User email
Statusset to To do
Priorityset to Lowest
Issue typeset to Task
Labels source listStep 1 output → Parameters → Labels
Labels → KeyStep 1 output → Parameters → Labels → Key
Labels → ValueStep 1 output → Parameters → Labels → Value
Due dateStep 1 output → Parameters → Due date
Detailed steps 9 steps

This is the first skill Casey can actually call mid-conversation — the point where Phase 5 stops being about the connection and starts being about what Casey can do with it. Tasks 5.3 and 5.4 follow the same shape, but without the confirmation step, because reading data doesn't carry the same risk as creating a ticket.

  • In your Genie's Edit mode, choose Add on a skill, then choose Create skill.
  • Name the skill and set its Location using the Config above.
  • Configure the trigger questions from the Config above.
  • Add the manual input fields from the Config above.
  • Add the manual output field from the Config above.
  • Above the Return response step, add an Action in app, choose Kanban, then choose Create Kanban ticket using this recipe's connection.
  • In the action setup, select Project key, Summary, and Labels, then expand optional fields to also select Description, Status, Priority, Issue type, and Due date.
  • Map each field from the Config above, then choose Apply changes.
  • On the Return response step, switch the Result field to Formula mode and drag the entire Step 2 output into it, then save and start the skill.
Verify chatting with Casey about an unresolved IT problem prompts a ticket-creation confirmation, and the resulting ticket is visible in Kanban.
5.3

Create a skill to retrieve a Kanban ticket

An end user who already has a ticket number wants status, not a new ticket — Casey needs a second skill that only reads.

Overview

This skill wraps Get Kanban ticket by key and, unlike Task 5.2, needs no user confirmation — reading a ticket has no side effect. Formula mode on the Ticket details response field returns the entire Step 2 output rather than a single value.

Skill naming and trigger questions
FieldValue
NameWOW-XXX | [AGENT-STUDIO] : SKILL : 002 : Retrieve Kanban Ticket
LocationSkills folder
Require user confirmation before executing this skill?No
When should this skill run?When to use — to get details about a specific ticket by key. Do not use — when the user asks to list all tickets.
Input fieldTicket_Key — String, required
Output fieldticket_details — String, optional
Detailed steps 8 steps

Task 5.2 gave Casey a way to create tickets; this one gives it a way to check on one that already exists — the read half of the same Kanban relationship. Task 5.4 is the third and final skill, covering the case where an end user doesn't have a ticket key to search by at all.

  • In your Genie's Edit mode, add a skill and choose Create skill.
  • Name it and set its Location using the Config above.
  • Configure the trigger questions and fields from the Config above.
  • Above the Return response step, add an Action in app, choose Kanban, then choose Get Kanban ticket by key using this recipe's connection.
  • Map the Ticket key parameter from Step 1 output into the action's Ticket key field.
  • On the Return response step, select the Ticket details field, switch to Formula mode, and drag the entire Step 2 output into it.
  • Save and start the skill.
  • Switch back to Workato Go, start a new thread with your Genie, and provide an existing ticket key when asking for its details.
Verify Casey returns the correct ticket details when given an existing ticket key.
5.4

Create a skill to list all Kanban tickets

Casey can create a ticket and look one up — the last gap is answering "what's open right now?" without a ticket key at all.

Overview

This third skill wraps List Kanban tickets, again with no confirmation required, and returns the entire ticket list through the same Formula-mode pattern used in Task 5.3. It reuses the same Kanban connection as your other two skills, so the tickets it lists are scoped to whatever the IT Service Account can see.

Skill naming and trigger questions
FieldValue
NameWOW-XXX | [AGENT-STUDIO] : SKILL : 003 : List Kanban Tickets
LocationSkills folder
Require user confirmation before executing this skill?No
When should this skill run?When the user asks to see all the Kanban tickets they have access to.
Output fieldlist_of_tickets — String, optional
Detailed steps 8 steps

Between Task 5.2's create and Task 5.3's single-ticket lookup, this is the gap that's left: an end user who wants to know what's open without naming a specific ticket. With all three skills built, Casey now has the same read/write range over Kanban a person on the IT team would have — Phase 6 is about refining how those skills describe themselves, not adding new ones.

  • In your Genie's Edit mode, add a skill and choose Create skill.
  • Name it and set its Location using the Config above.
  • Configure the trigger question and field from the Config above.
  • Above the Return response step, add an Action in app, choose Kanban, then choose List Kanban tickets using this recipe's connection.
  • On the Return response step, select the List of tickets field, switch to Formula mode, and drag the entire Tickets list from the recipe data menu into it.
  • Save and start the skill.
  • Switch back to Workato Go, start a new thread with your Genie, and ask it to show you the list of Kanban tickets.
  • Confirm the tickets shown match what the IT Service Account has access to in the Playground environment.
Verify Casey's list of tickets matches what the IT Service Account can see in Kanban.
Phase 6

AIRO

6.1

Update skill descriptions with AIRO

Three skills now carry the descriptions you wrote fast, in the middle of building — AIRO is how you tighten them without opening the skill editor by hand.

Overview

Chatting with AIRO from your project's top level, then from inside each skill, lets you ask it to explain and update descriptions in place. AIRO pauses the skill so it can write the change, and you verify the result before starting it again.

Detailed steps 8 steps

Every skill built in Phase 5 got a description written quickly, in the middle of building it — this is the pass where those descriptions get reviewed and tightened. It's also the last task in the lab, so once each skill is verified and restarted here, Casey is complete: grounded, connected, and ready to both answer and act for Anitech's IT team.

  • Close out of editing mode for your skills and Genie.
  • Navigate to the top-level folder of your project.
  • In the top left corner, start a new chat with AIRO.
  • Ask AIRO to explain what your Genie does.
  • Navigate to your project's Skills folder and open one of your skills.
  • Within the skill editor, ask AIRO to update the skill's top-level description. You may be prompted to stop the skill first.
  • Verify the updated description is accurate, then start the skill.
  • Repeat for each of the other skills used by your Genie.
Verify each skill's description reflects the update AIRO made, and every skill is running again after the edit.

Reflect

Now that Casey can answer, search, and act, consider what this means for the rest of Anitech's help desk.

  • If Anitech added a second knowledge base — say, a security-policy wiki — what would you need to change about how Casey decides which one to search?
  • The skills you built all share one connection authenticated as the IT Service Account. What would you change if a skill needed to act as the specific end user asking, instead of as that shared identity?
  • Task 5.2 requires confirmation before creating a ticket; Tasks 5.3 and 5.4 don't. What's the general rule you'd apply to a new skill you hadn't built yet?
  • AIRO updated a skill's description for you in Task 6.1. What would you still want a human to review before shipping that change to production?

Wrap-up

Casey now answers Anitech's IT questions from a real knowledge base, and can create, retrieve, and list Kanban tickets on an end user's behalf.

  • Casey saves the IT team real time. Every question it answers directly, and every issue it triages and escalates as a ticket instead of a person doing that by hand, is time the Anitech IT team gets back — the same 25% cut in ticket volume and roughly 80 hours a week this scenario is built around.
  • A Genie is four parts: Job Description, Chat Interface, Knowledge Bases, and Skills. The Job Description and Chat Interface let it hold a conversation and answer in character; Knowledge Bases give it something specific to answer from; Skills give it something it can actually do on the end user's behalf — together, that's what lets a Genie both answer and act.
  • A skill is a recipe underneath: Connections, Triggers, and Actions. Every skill you built authenticates through a Connection, decides when it should run through its Trigger questions, and does the work through an Action in the target app.
  • AIRO edits Genies and skills conversationally. Asking AIRO to explain what a Genie does, or to update a Genie's or skill's description, is the same edit path you used in Task 6.1 — no manual configuration editing required.

Appendix

Check these answers to Task 4.1's Kanban exploration questions once you've worked through them yourself — not before.

Question 1: In the IT Support Kanban board, what are the three possible statuses of a ticket? To do, Doing, Done.

Question 2: What are the five possible priorities of tickets? Lowest, Low, Medium, High, Highest.

Question 3: What are the names of the IT Support employees you see in the Quickchange Persona dropdown menu? Mira Solano, Sam Chen, Diego Ramos, Noor Aziz, and IT Service Account.

Question 4: Can all IT Support employees see all IT tickets? No. Each employee sees only the tickets where they're the Reporter or the Assignee.

Question 5: What is the difference between a Reporter and an Assignee? The Reporter is the IT Support employee who created the ticket. The Assignee is the employee the ticket is assigned to.

Question 6: Can the same IT Support employee be both the Reporter and the Assignee? Yes.

Question 7: If an end user creates a ticket through a Genie instead of an IT Support employee, what shows in the ticket's Reporter field? IT Service Account (SVC-0001).

Question 8: Of the three roles — Guest, Watcher, and Writer — which one can change a ticket's status? Only the Writer role.

Question 9: The most common Issue Type is "Task." True or false? True.

Question 10: A ticket's Labels field can hold more than one key/value pair. True or false? True.
